rules.instruction: When the description lists several activities that are carried out concurrently or in no stated order, and a later step starts only after all of them have completed: Model these activities as parallel branches: place a parallel gateway (split) before them, with one outgoing branch per activity and no conditions on the branches. Merge the branches with a matching parallel gateway (join) placed before the later step, so that step starts only after every branch has completed. Do not order the activities arbitrarily, do not use an exclusive gateway for the split or join, and do not let the later step follow any single branch.
rules.situation: the description says an activity is started in parallel with other work (for example with an explicit parallel qualifier) and is carried out separately for each of several items, and a later step starts only after all of these runs are finished

rules.instruction: When the description names an activity with a verb and object that covers a whole collection of items, and a later step concerns only one unit of that collection's output: Label the activity with the verb and object the description uses for the whole collection, not with the single unit that a later step concerns. Keep the later unit-level step as its own activity with its own label, placed after the collection-level activity it follows.
rules.situation: the description names an activity with a verb and object that covers a whole collection of items, and a later step concerns only one unit of that collection's output

rules.instruction: When the description states that a later activity can only begin after an external party has supplied the details or specifications that determine it (for example, requirements given to the producer before work starts): Model the act of obtaining or determining those details as its own activity (a user task performed by the responsible role) placed before the activities that depend on it, and connect it to them in sequence, rather than letting the dependent activities start directly from the start event.
